The cells that manufacture enamel are sensitive to systemic insults. Disruption in the production of enamel will result in a defect which may be micro or macroscopic. It is difficult to distinguish early decalcification from enamel defects, but this does not affect management. Enamel defects are associated with substantially increased risk of ECC.
Fluoridated Water, Fluoridated toothpaste, fluoride varnish, fluoride gels, foams and mouthwashes, Fluoride supplements

Dental fluorosis is a discoloring of the teeth due to chronic, excessive exposure to fluoride during tooth development. Fluorosis does not occur once teeth are fully developed. It is a cosmetic issue that does NOT affect systemic health. In its most common manifestation, it presents as a white mottling of the tooth enamel. It develops from exposure during tooth development to excessive fluoride at an intake of more than 0.06 milligrams per kilogram of body weight per day. Do not prescribe fluoride supplements without testing the fluoride content of the child’s water supply and a thorough history of all sources of water in the child’s diet, educate parents to use age appropriate amounts of toothpaste when brushing (for Susie a smear of toothpaste on her toothbrush). Fluoride varnish applied every two to four times per year is not a major risk factor for fluorosis since it is an episodic exposure, not chronic. Current clinical guidelines do not recommend use of fluoride supplements for children at low risk for dental caries because it increases the risk for fluorosis without adding significant prevention benefits.
